weekend_note: Hurricane Isaias is expected to make landfall on the northern Gulf Coast late Friday into early Saturday. The latest forecasts call for 4 to 8 inches of rain on the coast, gusts up to about 115 mph near Pensacola and a tornado threat, with conditions easing Saturday and a quieter, sunny Sunday and Monday. Evacuation is ordered for Zones A and B, including Pensacola Beach and Perdido Key. City events and permits are canceled through Sunday, and the Saenger, Festa Italiana, the Southern Tip Off, UWF football and the Blue Wahoos game are off. Treat anything else this weekend as unconfirmed until the organizer says otherwise. The picks below are next-week events and are subject to storm recovery; only the Ice Flyers game is indoors.

news.title: Isaias forecast: strong winds, heavy rain and surge for coastal Escambia
news.summary: FOX10 says the greatest coastal impacts are expected Friday night into early Saturday, with sustained winds of 65 to 85 mph on the coast, 4 to 8 inches of rain and 4 to 7 feet of surge in vulnerable areas. Inland Escambia could see gusts near 80 mph. Sunday is expected to be quieter, though flooding and surf may linger.

news.title: Hurricane warning covers Pensacola; evacuations underway
news.summary: The Weather Channel reports hurricane warnings along the Panhandle and a mandatory evacuation of Escambia Zones A and B, with shelters at the Pensacola Bay Center and Wedgewood Community Center. Fuel and store shelves were running short around Pensacola.

news.title: City and county closures for Isaias
news.summary: County offices are closed Friday. The City canceled event permits and rentals through Sunday, plus Saturday youth games, and county parks games for Oct 9 to 11 are postponed. ECUA customer service is closed Friday and Pensacola Beach water and sewer will be shut off after evacuation.

news.title: Airport, schools and colleges close
news.summary: WUWF's live updates list Pensacola International Airport closing at 10 AM Friday with no reopening date, Escambia schools closed Friday (Monday is already a holiday), Pensacola State College closed Friday and Saturday, and UWF classes canceled with normal operations expected Monday.

news.title: Gulf Islands National Seashore closed
news.summary: WUWF reports the seashore, including Fort Pickens, Perdido Key and Opal Beach, has been closed since Oct 7, and Highway 399 on Santa Rosa Island is to close Friday at a time not yet given.

news.title: Festa Italiana moved to mid-November
news.summary: Organizers postponed the festival to Nov 13 and 14 at Fountain Park, with free admission and 11 AM to 6 PM hours.

news.title: Weekend games and shows called off
news.summary: The Southern Tip Off at the Bay Center and UWF's home football game are canceled, as is the Blue Wahoos' FSU-Auburn exhibition. The Saenger lists its Thursday through Saturday shows as postponed.

coverage_note: Written around 3 AM Friday Oct 9, before Hurricane Isaias arrives, so conditions will change; confirm anything outdoors or on the beach with the organizer. Storm facts come from FOX10, The Weather Channel, WEAR and WUWF. The only National Weather Service page that loaded was the marine point forecast, which shows hurricane conditions Friday night and sunny weather Sunday through Tuesday, so the land highs, lows and rain chances for Oct 9 to 14 are carried over from the Oct 8 NWS point forecast and Sunday onward rain chances remain a 10 percent placeholder; no Oct 15 forecast was available. Event details are unchanged from last night because no organizers had posted new storm updates in the sources that could be read; the Saenger, Bay Center, UWF and Blue Wahoos cancellations remain confirmed. Many event pages (City of Pensacola, Visit Pensacola, Saenger and Facebook-only listings) could not be opened this run. NorthEscambia.com would not load, so north and west Escambia and Gonzalez coverage is thin and limited to county library classes already listed. Restaurant statuses are unchanged; Pelican Bar and Grill and Casa Luvia remain unconfirmed.
